Adding risk scores

Source: vignettes/adding-columns.Rmd
adding-columns.Rmd

sRtr adds published donor and candidate scores to a data frame as new columns. Each function reads SRTR column names, so it works on a file loaded with load_srtr_file(). The examples here use a few made-up rows, so they run on this site.

library(sRtr)

The scores

Function Adds For Columns come from
add_kdpi() KDRI and KDPI Deceased kidney donors DONOR_DECEASED, or TX_KI
add_epts() EPTS Adult kidney candidates or recipients CAND_KIPA (at listing) or TX_KI (at transplant)
add_donor_egfr() Donor eGFR (CKD-EPI) Donors DONOR_DECEASED, or DONOR_LIVE with creatinine = "DON_KI_CREAT_PREOP"
add_lkdpi() LKDPI Living donor kidney transplants DONOR_LIVE joined to TX_KI
add_pdri() PDRI Pancreas and kidney-pancreas transplants TX_PA or TX_KP
add_pvr() Pulmonary vascular resistance Heart, lung and heart-lung candidates CAND_THOR (at listing) or TX_HR, TX_LU, TX_HL (at transplant)

Each function’s help page lists the exact input columns, the codes it reads and the paper or OPTN guide that defines the score.

Which mapping table: KDPI and EPTS

KDPI and EPTS are percentiles. The raw score (KDRI or raw EPTS) is mapped to a percentile with a table that OPTN publishes each year, built from the donors or candidates of a reference year. The same donor can get a different KDPI from a different table. sRtr stores the tables in optn_mapping_tables.

A made-up donor, recovered on five dates:

donor <- data.frame(
  DON_AGE = 52, DON_HGT_CM = 183, DON_WGT_KG = 81,
  DON_HIST_HYPERTEN = 2, DON_HIST_DIAB = 1, DON_CAD_DON_COD = 2,
  DON_CREAT = 1.7, DON_NON_HR_BEAT = "Y", DON_RACE = 2000,
  DON_ANTI_HCV = "N"
)
donors <- donor[rep(1, 5), ]
donors$DON_RECOV_DT <- as.Date(
  c("2010-03-01", "2015-03-01", "2023-03-01", "2025-01-15", "2025-08-01")
)

The table argument chooses the table:

  • "latest" (the default) uses the newest stored table for every row.
  • "in_force" uses, for each row, the table OPTN was using on the donor recovery date (DON_RECOV_DT), not the transplant date.
  • A label such as "2018" uses that table for every row. The table must match the formula: "2018" needs version = "rao2009".
kdpi <- add_kdpi(donors, version = "rao2009", table = "in_force")
#> Warning: No stored rao2009 KDPI table was in force on the recovery date for 3 rows; KDPI
#> set to NA.
#> ℹ Stored rao2009 tables: "2012", "2013", "2014", "2015", "2016", "2017",
#>   "2018", "2019", "2020", "2021", "2022", and "2023". See
#>   `optn_mapping_tables$effective` for the dates.
data.frame(
  recovered = kdpi$DON_RECOV_DT,
  KDPI = kdpi$KDPI,
  table = attr(kdpi$KDPI, "optn_table")
)
#>    recovered KDPI table
#> 1 2010-03-01   NA  <NA>
#> 2 2015-03-01   84  2013
#> 3 2023-03-01   79  2021
#> 4 2025-01-15   NA  <NA>
#> 5 2025-08-01   NA  <NA>

The rows with no KDPI are not errors in the donor’s data. In March 2010 no KDPI table was yet in force, and from 2024-10-31 OPTN used the refit formula (version = "refit2024", the default), whose tables are separate:

refit <- add_kdpi(donors, table = "in_force")
#> Warning: No stored refit2024 KDPI table was in force on the recovery date for 4 rows;
#> KDPI set to NA.
#> ℹ Stored refit2024 tables: "2024" and "current". See
#>   `optn_mapping_tables$effective` for the dates.
data.frame(
  recovered = refit$DON_RECOV_DT,
  KDPI = refit$KDPI,
  table = attr(refit$KDPI, "optn_table")
)
#>    recovered KDPI table
#> 1 2010-03-01   NA  <NA>
#> 2 2015-03-01   NA  <NA>
#> 3 2023-03-01   NA  <NA>
#> 4 2025-01-15   79  2024
#> 5 2025-08-01   NA  <NA>

The last row has no KDPI either way: OPTN has not archived the table it used from 2025-05-21. sRtr warns each time a row gets no table.

The start date of each table is in optn_mapping_tables$effective, with its basis. Where OPTN published a date, that date is used. Otherwise the start is June 1 of the following year, the deadline in OPTN policy, which is a convention:

eff <- optn_mapping_tables$effective
eff[eff$score == "kdpi", c("label", "kdri_formula", "effective_from")]
#>          label kdri_formula effective_from
#> 13        2010      rao2009     2011-06-01
#> 14        2011      rao2009     2012-06-01
#> 15        2012      rao2009     2013-06-01
#> 16        2013      rao2009     2014-06-01
#> 17        2014      rao2009     2015-06-01
#> 18        2015      rao2009     2016-06-01
#> 19        2016      rao2009     2017-06-01
#> 20        2017      rao2009     2018-06-01
#> 21        2018      rao2009     2019-06-01
#> 22        2019      rao2009     2020-06-01
#> 23        2020      rao2009     2021-06-01
#> 24        2021      rao2009     2022-06-01
#> 25        2022      rao2009     2023-06-01
#> 26        2023      rao2009     2024-05-29
#> 27        2024    refit2024     2024-10-31
#> 28 2024-donors    refit2024     2025-05-21
#> 29     current    refit2024     2026-06-01

A missing KDPI from a table can have three causes:

  • The table is not stored. OPTN has not archived the 2024-donors table, in force from 2025-05-21.
  • The table is stored but incomplete. The 2010 and 2011 tables lack the scaling factor that turns KDRI into a percentile, so they give no KDPI.
  • The table lacks what one donor needs. The 2012 and 2013 tables do not print the share of reference donors with hypertension or diabetes, so a donor with unknown history (code 998) gets no KDPI from them under the default unknown_history = "optn".

sRtr says so each time, in a warning or a message.

add_epts() works the same way, on the listing date or the transplant date (at = "listing" or "transplant").

Missing and unknown inputs

A missing or unknown input usually gives a missing score. Each function documents its exceptions, and a few are options:

Function Input Default Option
add_kdpi() Unknown hypertension or diabetes history (998) Weighted by the reference donors’ share, as in the OPTN calculator unknown_history = "na"
add_kdpi() Unknown or pending HCV, Rao 2009 only Counted as negative, as in the OPTN calculator none
add_epts() Unknown diabetes (998) Missing EPTS unknown_diabetes = "no", a convention
add_epts() Missing dialysis start date 0 years if not on dialysis, else missing missing_dialysis_date = "zero", a convention
add_epts(), add_donor_egfr() Age under 18 Missing adults_only = FALSE
add_pdri() Any missing input, including race Missing PDRI. A missing BMI is first computed from height and weight. mean_impute = TRUE: continuous inputs take the mean of their dplyr group (of all rows if ungrouped), and missing yes/no terms count as 0, for the calculation only

Decide these before computing scores, and report the choice. To see how many rows lose a score, count them:

unknown <- donor
unknown$DON_HIST_DIAB <- 998
both <- rbind(donor, unknown)
data.frame(
  diabetes = c("no", "unknown"),
  default = as.numeric(add_kdpi(both)$KDPI),
  na = as.numeric(add_kdpi(both, unknown_history = "na")$KDPI)
)
#> KDRI is missing for 1 row with a missing or unusable input.
#>   diabetes default na
#> 1       no      67 67
#> 2  unknown      73 NA

Codes or labels

The functions read raw codes and the factor labels that load_srtr_file() applies, so a file loaded either way works. A format’s own missing code (".", labelled "Missing") counts as missing. See Missing data for what the other unknown codes mean.

What has been checked

Function Checked against its source Run on real SAFs
add_kdpi() KDRI for the donors in the OPTN KDPI guides (refit and Rao 2009) Yes: KDPI range on one release’s DONOR_DECEASED
add_epts() Raw EPTS and the 2024 table for the candidates in the OPTN EPTS guide Not yet
add_donor_egfr() The equations in Inker et al. 2021, Table 2 Yes: values on one release’s DONOR_DECEASED
add_lkdpi() The equation in Massie et al. 2016 Not yet
add_pdri() The formula, and rounded examples from the paper (#93); two copies of the paper print different BMI coefficients Not yet
add_pvr() The definition Not yet

A check against the source shows agreement on the examples checked. A run on real SAFs shows the function reads the real columns and codes. Neither shows that a score matches published cohort results: that agreement has not been established for any of these scores.

The KDPI guide prints 63% for its Rao 2009 example, but the stored 2018 table maps that donor’s KDRI to 83%. sRtr gives 83, and the test records the difference.
